questiontext.text: Which data structure does the shunting-yard algorithm use to hold operators during infix → postfix conversion?

feedback.text: Correct — operators are pushed and popped on a stack.
The output can be a queue, but operators are held on a stack.
No tree is needed for the linear scan.
Operator precedence ordering needs a stack, not a hash table.

generalfeedback.text: The shunting-yard algorithm uses a stack to hold operators while scanning the infix expression.

questiontext.text: While scanning the infix expression left to right, what do you do when you read an operand?

answer.text: Output it directly to the postfix expression

feedback.text: Correct — operands go straight to the output.

answer.text: Push it onto the operator stack

feedback.text: Only operators and parentheses are pushed; operands are output.
Operands must appear in the output.

answer.text: Pop the stack until it is empty

feedback.text: That is not done for a plain operand.

generalfeedback.text: Operands are appended directly to the output; the stack only manages operators and parentheses.

questiontext.text: When you read a left parenthesis ( during infix → postfix conversion, what do you do?

feedback.text: Correct — the left parenthesis is pushed and acts as a barrier.

answer.text: Output it immediately to the postfix expression

feedback.text: Parentheses never appear in the postfix output.

answer.text: Pop the stack until it is empty

feedback.text: That is not done on a left parenthesis.
You must push it so the matching right parenthesis can find it.

generalfeedback.text: A left parenthesis is pushed onto the stack and later removed when its matching right parenthesis is processed.

questiontext.text: For a left-associative operator whose precedence equals the stack-top operator, before pushing you should:

answer.text: Pop the stack-top operator to the output first

feedback.text: Correct — equal precedence with left associativity means pop before push.

answer.text: Push the new operator without popping

feedback.text: That would be right-associative behavior, not left.
Operators are never discarded.

answer.text: Output the operator's operands a second time

feedback.text: Operands are output once, when scanned.

generalfeedback.text: Left associativity: pop operators of higher OR equal precedence before pushing the current operator.

questiontext.text: On encountering a right parenthesis ), you pop operators to the output until the matching ( is removed.

feedback.text: Correct — pop until the matching left parenthesis, which is discarded.
That is exactly how parentheses are resolved during conversion.

questiontext.text: Postfix (Reverse Polish) expressions require parentheses to express operator precedence.

feedback.text: Postfix is unambiguous, so parentheses are never needed.
Correct — RPN encodes precedence in operator order and needs no parentheses.

questiontext.text: The shunting-yard algorithm holds pending operators on a ______.

feedback.text: Correct.
Correct.

questiontext.text: Which statements about infix → postfix conversion are true? (select all that apply)

answer.text: Before pushing a left-associative operator, pop operators of higher or equal precedence

feedback.text: Yes — this preserves correct precedence and associativity.

answer.text: Operands are appended directly to the output

feedback.text: Yes — operands go straight to the output.

answer.text: A queue holds the operators awaiting output

feedback.text: No — operators are held on a stack.

answer.text: The resulting postfix expression needs parentheses to disambiguate precedence

feedback.text: No — postfix is unambiguous and needs no parentheses.

generalfeedback.text: Operators live on a stack, popped by precedence/associativity; operands stream to output; postfix needs no parentheses.
